title: Mast-o Musir
subtitle: yoghurt with shallots
excerpt: Mast-o Musir is a simple Persian yoghurt dip made with soaked wild shallots, rose water and mint. It is cooling, slightly pungent and eaten alongside every Persian meal. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Mast-o Musir is made with musir, wild Persian shallots that are soaked before use to mellow their intensity. It is a staple side dish at Persian restaurants and family tables.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 days ahead. Keep covered in the fridge. The onion mellow over time.

glossaryTerms.definition: Wild Persian shallots, small and pungent, traditionally soaked overnight in cold water to mellow their bite before being stirred into yoghurt.
The Persian word for yoghurt, creamy and tangy, a staple of the Iranian table eaten at almost every meal.

The rose water is optional but traditional. It adds a subtle floral note that balances the sharpness of the onion. Use sparingly.

items.prepNote: very finely diced, rinsed in cold water and drained

content.text: Dice the onion very finely. Place the diced onion in a small bowl of cold water and leave for 10 minutes. This removes the harsh sulphur compounds and makes the flavour milder.
Drain the onion thoroughly and pat dry with kitchen paper. Any residual water will make the yoghurt thin.
Place the yoghurt in a bowl. Add the drained onion and chopped mint. Stir to combine. Add the rose water if using and stir through.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. The onion and mint flavour the yoghurt as they sit together.
Transfer to a shallow serving bowl. Drizzle with olive oil and scatter with dried chilli flakes if using. Serve cold alongside Persian rice, stews or kebabs.

attrs.problem: Onion flavour is still too sharp
attrs.solution: Rinse the onion for longer, up to 30 minutes in cold water, changing the water once. You can also use a very small amount of onion and increase the mint to compensate.
Ensure the onion is completely drained and patted dry before mixing in. Use a thick full-fat yoghurt rather than a pourable variety. Strain Greek yoghurt through muslin for an even thicker result.
Add less next time. Rose water concentrations vary significantly by brand. Half a teaspoon is already at the upper end. A drop or two from a pipette is enough from a concentrated brand.

content.text: Mast-o Musir appears on the table at every Persian restaurant in Iran. It is served alongside kababs, rice and other cold dishes as part of the spread that precedes the main meal. Wild musir shallots are sold dried in Iranian grocery shops outside Iran. They are soaked overnight to rehydrate and soften before mixing into the yoghurt. The rose water version is the most traditional and elegant.
